'''Ask Aak''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] who represented [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] during the final decade of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

==Biography==
The successor of the late [[Aks Moe/Legends|Aks Moe]], Ask Aak was a vocal proponent of the [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]], and went on to support the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] effort in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] to come. When a [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]], commissioned by a [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Jedi Master]] ten years earlier, was discovered by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Aak pressed for its use.

[[File:Bail_and_Ask_Aak.jpg|thumb|left|Aak with Bail Organa]]
At some point before the Clone Wars, a [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] named [[Tahbotza]] attempted to blackmail Ask Aak's staff. For this, Aak placed a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on Tahbotza's head. Aak, as well as his colleague, Aks Moe, placed a bounty on two other Dugs, named [[Ghazdik Jah]] and [[Mazanga]] for the murder of their special [[Aide/Legends|assistants]]. Aak also wanted [[Zap'Ulga]] for connections to a series of raids on [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] carrying relief supplies to [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]]. Aak also placed a bounty on another Dug called [[Xucaabo]] for falling heavily on debt. All of these bounties were claimed by [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]].

A strong supporter of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], he was more progressive and action-oriented than many [[Loyalist/Legends|Loyalist]] Senators, every bit as outspoken as his predecessor. He heavily criticized the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], blaming them for not preventing Aks Moe's [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]], and later for the disastrous [[Battle of Parcelus Minor|battle]] of [[Parcelus Minor/Legends|Parcelus Minor]]. He was very critical of their role in the war, especially during the first few [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of the conflict, and openly questioned the capability of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Oppo Rancisis/Legends|Oppo Rancisis]]. He was also one of the main proponents of the [[Enhanced Security and Enforcement Act]].

He was present in the Senate in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] when Palpatine proclaimed its New Order and replaced the Republic with the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Around [[11 BBY/Legends|11 BBY]], Senator Aak sent three men on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] to kidnap eight-year-old [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], so he could use the young [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] to blackmail her adoptive father, [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]]. However, former Jedi [[Ferus Olin]], who was tasked to watch over Leia, stopped the thugs and used a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] on them to make them leave the [[Planet/Legends|planet]].<ref name="Rebel Force: Hostage">''[[Rebel Force: Hostage]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[Steven Boyle]] played Ask Aak in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']]. In [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], the role went to [[Paul Spence]].<ref name="DB" /> Ask Aak later appeared in the webcomic ''[[The Clone Wars: Procedure]]'' by [[Pablo Hidalgo]]. That a [[Unidentified Gran worker|Gran]] was seen working in the [[Bormus testing facility/Legends|Bormus testing facility]] was intended by Hidalgo to show that Ask Aak put his followers and friends into places of influence.<ref name="PH">{{JCFCite|url=posts/29267113|board=Literature|thread=Clone Wars web comics: Official thread|user=[[Pablo Hidalgo|Pabawan]]|date=2008-10-07|time=1:19 PM}}</ref>
